entries.jp: 雨がやむ気配はないですね\n夜まで降るのかも
entries.en:
There's no sign of
the rain letting
up. It may keep
falling until
night.

entries.jp: じっとするのは退屈だし\nどこかへ出てパッと\n遊びたいなぁ～
entries.en:
Sittin' around is
borin'. I wanna
head out
somewhere and
have some real
fun~

entries.jp: 子供かおまえは\nわざわざ濡れに行くこたぁ\nねえだろ
entries.en:
What are you, a
kid? No need to
go out of your
way to get
soaked.

entries.jp: 龍馬くん　退屈だったら\nヱゲレスの書物でも\n読みますか？
entries.en:
Ryoma-kun, if
you're bored,
would you like to
read an English
book?

entries.jp: わしはヱゲレスの書物より\nヱゲレスの生のロックを\n聴いてみたいっ！
entries.en:
Instead of
English books, I'd
rather hear real
live English rock!

entries.jp: どうせエゲレス語が\n読めねえんだろ
entries.en: You can't read\nEnglish anyway,\ncan you?

entries.jp: わしだって少しは読めるぞ\n掘った芋弄るな！　とか
entries.en:
I can read a little,
I'll have ya know!
Like, "Wotta time
izzit nao!"

entries.jp: なんだそりゃ\nわけわからねぇ
entries.en: What's that\nsupposed to be?\nMakes no sense.

entries.jp: そういえば龍馬くんって\n土佐にいた時はどうしてた\nのです？
entries.en:
Speaking of
which,
Ryoma-kun, what
did you do back
when you were in
Tosa?

entries.jp: 大自然に囲まれて\n楽しく遊んでたなー
entries.en: Ran around havin'\nfun out in the\ngreat outdoors!

entries.jp: 勉学はしなかったのかよ
entries.en: You didn't study\nor anything?

entries.jp: 勉学も剣術もしてたし\nいっぱいと遊ぶことも\n忘れんかったな
entries.en:
I did my studies
and my
swordsmanship,
and I never
forgot to play
plenty, neither.

entries.jp: 土佐の遊びって\n私達の遊びとは違うのか\n興味がありますね
entries.en:
I wonder if games
in Tosa are
different from
ours. How
fascinating.

entries.jp: よく聞いてくれた\n土佐の遊びはわいるどで\nえきさいてぃんぐじゃ
entries.en: Glad ya asked!\nTosa games are\nwild 'n' excitin'!

entries.jp: 土佐はなーんもねえだろ\n自然は豊かそうだけどな
entries.en:
There's nothing
in Tosa. Plenty of
nature, I'll give
you that.

entries.jp: 鍾乳洞で探検遊びして\n中で迷子になって二日ほど\n迷路を彷徨ったなー
entries.en:
I played explorer
in a limestone
cave, got lost
inside, and
wandered that
maze for two
days or so!

entries.jp: 危ないですね……\nでもよく助かりましたね
entries.en: How dangerous...\nBut it's a wonder\nyou were rescued.

entries.jp: 腹が減って　腹が減って\nそしたら美味そうな匂いが\n漂ってきたんじゃ
entries.en:
I was hungry, so
hungry... And
then this tasty
smell came
driftin' my way.

entries.jp: 鍾乳洞の中でか？
entries.en: Inside a cave?

entries.jp: そうなんじゃ\nこりゃたまらんと\n匂いの方へ歩いたんじゃ
entries.en:
Yep! I couldn't
stand it, so I
followed my nose
toward the smell.

entries.jp: なんとそれは鍾乳洞の\n入り口近くの茶店から漂う\n団子の匂いだったんじゃ！
entries.en:
And wouldn't ya
know, it was the
smell of dango
driftin' from a
teahouse by the
cave entrance!

entries.jp: 団子の匂いに誘われて\n助かったってことですか
entries.en:
So you were
saved by
following the
smell of dango?

entries.jp: そういうことじゃ\nわはは
entries.en: That's about the\nsize of it!\nWahaha!

entries.jp: わははじゃねーだろ\n動物かよおまえは
entries.en: Don't "wahaha"\nme. What are you,\nan animal?

entries.jp: 松蔭先生も鍾乳洞で\n迷子になったらしいけど\n命懸けすぎだろ
entries.en:
I heard
Shoin-sensei got
lost in a cave too,
but that's way too
much risking your
life.

entries.jp: 土佐の鍾乳洞というと……\n龍河洞（りゅうがどう）\nですよね
entries.en:
A limestone cave
in Tosa... That
would be
Ryugado,
wouldn't it?

entries.jp: そうじゃ\nさすがセンセー\n物知りじゃ
entries.en: That's right!\nSensei sure knows\nhis stuff!

entries.jp: あと　土佐と言えば\nカツオと鯨が有名ですね
entries.en:
And speaking of
Tosa, it's famous
for its bonito and
whales.

entries.jp: そうじゃ　カツオと鯨！
entries.en: That's right,\nbonito and\nwhales!

entries.jp: カツオは旬になると\n漁船がカツオで真っ黒い\n山になるんじゃ
entries.en:
In bonito season,
the fishing boats
come back piled
with black
mountains of
bonito!

entries.jp: そんなに獲れるのかよ\n話盛りすぎだろ
entries.en:
They catch that
many? You're
laying it on way
too thick.

entries.jp: 大げさじゃないって\n船が半分ぐらい沈みかける\nほどに獲れるんじゃ
entries.en:
I ain't
exaggeratin'!
They catch so
many, the boats
are half sinkin'!

entries.jp: わしはカツオが好きでな\n漁から戻ってくるのを\n心待ちにしてたぜよ
entries.en:
I love bonito, see.
I'd wait and wait
for the boats to
come back in.

entries.jp: へえ　カツオ漁ってのは\n網でやるのか？
entries.en: Huh. So do they\ncatch bonito with\nnets?

entries.jp: よくぞ聞いてくれた！\n網なんぞ使わん\n土佐の漁師は一本釣りじゃ
entries.en:
Glad ya asked! No
nets! Tosa
fishermen use
pole-and-line, one
fish at a time!

entries.jp: 一本釣りなんて\n効率が悪くねえか？
entries.en: Isn't one fish at a\ntime kind of\ninefficient?

entries.jp: カツオは鯨と一緒に\n泳ぐから網が使えん\n一本釣りが基本なんじゃ
entries.en:
Bonito swim with
whales, so ya
can't use nets.
Pole-and-line's
the way it's done.

entries.jp: 勇壮な海の男達が\n竿一本でカツオを釣る！\n海でもロックなんじゃ！
entries.en:
Brave men of the
sea, landin' bonito
with nothin' but a
pole! That's rock,
even out on the
sea!

entries.jp: 素晴らしそうですね\nカツオの一本釣りは\n私も見てみたいですよ
entries.en:
That sounds
wonderful. I'd
love to see
pole-and-line
bonito fishing
myself.

entries.jp: わしも船に乗った\nことがあるぜよ
entries.en: I've been out on\nthe boats myself,\ny'know!

entries.jp: 龍馬くんも\n釣れたんですか？
entries.en: Did you catch one\ntoo, Ryoma-kun?

entries.jp: でっかいカツオが掛かって\nわし対カツオの一本勝負に\nなった！
entries.en:
I hooked a huge
bonito, and it
turned into a
one-on-one
showdown, me
against the
bonito!

entries.jp: ものすごい力で逃げようと\nするカツオと　釣り上げて\n食おうとするわしの勝負
entries.en:
A showdown
between a bonito
fightin' with all
its might to get
away and me,
reelin' it in to eat
it!

entries.jp: カツオは命懸けだからな
entries.en: That bonito was\nfightin' for its\nlife, after all.

entries.jp: あと少しでカツオの鼻面が\n海面にみえて来た！\nってところまで頑張った
entries.en:
I hung on till I
could just about
see its snout
breakin' the
surface!

entries.jp: 釣り上げたんですね！
entries.en: So you reeled it\nin!

entries.jp: いや　わしがカツオに\n釣られて海へドボンじゃ\nわはははは
entries.en:
Nope! The bonito
reeled ME in, and
in the sea I went,
splash!
Wahahahaha!

entries.jp: そんなこっちゃねーかと\n思ってたらそのまんまか
entries.en:
I figured it'd be
something like
that, and that's
exactly what it
was.

entries.jp: 海に落ちたわしを\n漁師が一本釣りで\n釣り上げてくれてなー
entries.en:
Then a fisherman
reeled me outta
the sea with his
pole!

entries.jp: さすが土佐の漁師\nわしの帯に張りを引っかけ\n釣り上げたってわけじゃ
entries.en:
That's a Tosa
fisherman for ya.
He hooked my
sash and reeled
me right on up.

entries.jp: すごい体験です　龍馬くん\nヱゲレスの本よりも\nドキドキしますよ！
entries.en:
What an
incredible
experience,
Ryoma-kun! It's
more thrilling
than any English
book!

entries.jp: わははは\n土佐の子供はわいるどで\nえきさいてぃんぐ！
entries.en: Wahahaha! Tosa\nkids are wild 'n'\nexcitin'!

entries.jp: あと　わしは鯨に飲まれた\nことがあるぜよ！
entries.en: And I got\nswallowed by a\nwhale once, too!

entries.jp: ええっ \n鯨って人を食べないはず\nですけど
entries.en:
Whaaat? But
whales aren't
supposed to eat
people...

entries.jp: それが食われたんじゃ\nセンセー
entries.en: Well, this one ate\nme, Sensei.

entries.jp: でっかい鯨に\nぱくっと飲まれて\n死ぬかと思ったぜよ！
entries.en:
A huge whale
swallowed me in
one gulp! I
thought I was a
goner!

entries.jp: ウソつけ　この野郎
entries.en: Quit lying, you\njerk.

entries.jp: ウソじゃないって\nガチで恐ろしい目に\n遭ったんじゃ
entries.en:
It ain't a lie! I
went through
somethin'
seriously
terrifyin'!

entries.jp: 今思い出しても\n背筋がゾクゾクする\n恐ろしい体験だった～
entries.en:
Even now, just
rememberin' it
sends chills down
my spine. What a
terrifyin' time
that was~

entries.jp: 詳しく話して下さい\n龍馬くん\nすごく興味があります
entries.en:
Please tell me the
details,
Ryoma-kun. I'm
very interested.

entries.jp: おいおい　桂さんよ\n本気にしてるのか
entries.en:
Hey, hey,
Katsura-san.
You're actually
buying this?

entries.jp: まあシンディも聞け
entries.en: Aw, just listen,\nShindy.

entries.jp: ありゃあ　わしがまだ\n五つか六つの頃だった
entries.en: It was back when\nI was only five or\nsix.

entries.jp: 今日は大漁じゃという\n知らせを聞いて\n港へ見に行ったんだ
entries.en:
I heard word
there was a big
catch that day, so
I went down to
the harbor to see.

entries.jp: そういう知らせが届く\nようになっているんですか
entries.en: Does news like\nthat reach you,\nthen?

entries.jp: 漁港が近いしな　近所に\n漁師さんが住んでいて\n家族に話が届くぜよ
entries.en:
The fishin' port's
close by, and
fishermen live in
the
neighborhood, so
word gets to the
families.

entries.jp: 港へ駆けつけたら\nでっかい鯨がいくつも\n揚がっていたんだ
entries.en:
When I ran down
to the harbor,
there were a
bunch of huge
whales hauled up.

entries.jp: こりゃでかい鯨だ\n大人でもひと飲みに\nするだろうと思ってな
entries.en:
"Now that's a big
whale," I thought.
"Bet it could
swallow a
grown-up in one
gulp."

entries.jp: そんなに大きな鯨が\n揚がるんですね
entries.en: They really haul\nup whales that\nbig?

entries.jp: そりゃあもう\n一人ではとうてい\n食えん大きさじゃ！
entries.en:
You bet! Way too
big for one fella
to ever eat by
himself!

entries.jp: どこの世界に鯨一頭\n一人で食う奴がいるんだよ\n大人でも無理だろうが
entries.en:
Where in the
world is there a
guy who'd eat a
whole whale
alone? Even a
grown man
couldn't do it.

entries.jp: そうですか？\n干し肉にすれば\nしばらく保存できますよ
entries.en:
Is that so? If you
dried the meat, it
would keep for
quite a while.

entries.jp: あのなあ　桂さん\n食い終わる前に飽きるだろ
entries.en:
Look,
Katsura-san.
You'd get sick of
it before you
finished.

entries.jp:
わはは
センセーは天然入ってる
から　シンディも
苦労するなぁ
entries.en:
Wahaha! Sensei's
got a bit of a
natural-born
airhead in him.
Must be rough on
ya, Shindy.

entries.jp: 天然のおまえが言うな！\n桂さんも何か言ってやれよ
entries.en:
Don't you say
that, you
natural-born
airhead!
Katsura-san, say
something to him!

entries.jp: んー　だから龍馬くんと\n息が合うんですね
entries.en:
Hmm... So that's
why Ryoma-kun
and I get along so
well.

entries.jp: なんかもう　どうでも\nよくなってくるような\n反応だな　桂さんよ
entries.en:
That's the kind of
answer that
makes me stop
caring about
anything,
Katsura-san.

entries.jp: それで龍馬くん\nどうして鯨に飲まれたのか\n聞かせてもらいたいです
entries.en:
So, Ryoma-kun,
I'd love to hear
how you got
swallowed by a
whale.

entries.jp: そうそう　その話！\n鯨の中でも一番でかい奴の\n鼻面に近付いた時だ
entries.en:
Right, right, that
story! It was when
I got close to the
snout of the
biggest whale of
all.

entries.jp: わしの背丈を超える口が\nがばーっと開いたんぜよ！
entries.en:
A mouth taller
than me opened
up wide --
*gwaaah*!

entries.jp: こりゃいかん　食われると\n思って逃げようとした\nその時じゃ！
entries.en:
I thought, "Uh-oh,
it's gonna eat me!"
and tried to run,
and right then!

entries.jp: ドキドキしますね　晋作
entries.en: How thrilling,\nShinsaku.

entries.jp: 話半分に聞いてろよ\n桂さんは\nで　どうなったんだよ？
entries.en:
Only believe half
of it, Katsura-san.
So? What
happened?

entries.jp: わしの足が縄に絡まって\n動けんところを\n鯨の口がぱくっと！
entries.en:
My foot got
tangled in a rope,
and while I was
stuck there, the
whale's mouth
went *chomp*!

entries.jp: うわー\nそれは怖いですね
entries.en: Oh my, how\nfrightening.

entries.jp: 頭から飲まれたんじゃ\nまともに息も出来んし\n恐ろしかった……
entries.en:
It swallowed me
headfirst! I
couldn't hardly
breathe. It was
terrifyin'...

entries.jp: 鯨の口の中って\n想像も出来ませんね
entries.en:
I can't even
imagine the
inside of a
whale's mouth.

entries.jp: 口の中が生臭くて\nそりゃあもう臭い臭い
entries.en:
It was all fishy in
there. And boy,
did it stink, stink,
stink!

entries.jp: あたりまえだろ\nというか息できないのに\nなんで匂いがわかるんだよ
entries.en:
Obviously. And
how'd you smell
anything if you
couldn't breathe?

entries.jp: 逃げ出した時に\n着物が臭かったんじゃ
entries.en: My kimono stank\nwhen I got out!

entries.jp: 私の興味はそこですよ\nどうやって助かったんです
entries.en:
That's the part
I'm curious about.
How were you
saved?

entries.jp: 不幸中の幸いか\n腹の中に先客がいた
entries.en:
Call it a stroke of
luck: somebody
was already in its
belly ahead of me.

entries.jp: 龍馬くんの他にも\n飲まれた人がいましたか！
entries.en:
Someone besides
you had been
swallowed,
Ryoma-kun!?

entries.jp: ごっつい刃物を持った\n漁師のおっさんが\n腹の中を切り始めたんじゃ
entries.en:
A burly fisherman
with a big ol'
blade started
cuttin' up its belly
from the inside!

entries.jp: 鯨が痛がって暴れたんで\nわしは吐き出されたんじゃ
entries.en:
The whale
thrashed around
in pain, and it
spat me right out!

entries.jp: すごい体験です　龍馬くん\n私も体験してみたいです
entries.en:
What an
incredible
experience,
Ryoma-kun. I'd
like to experience
it too.

entries.jp: ねえ晋作　紀州に行けば\n鯨漁を見られますよね？
entries.en:
Say, Shinsaku, if
we went to Kishu,
we could see
whaling, couldn't
we?

entries.jp: あのなあ　桂さん\n龍馬の話を鵜呑みにするな\nよ～く考えてみろ
entries.en:
Look,
Katsura-san. Don't
swallow Ryoma's
story whole.
Think it over real
hard.

entries.jp: 漁港に揚げられた鯨が\n生きてると思うか？\n暴れて大変だぞ？
entries.en:
You think a whale
hauled up at a
fishing port is
still alive? It'd
thrash all over
the place,
wouldn't it?

entries.jp: ああ　そういえばそうです\n鯨はとどめを刺してから\n陸に運ぶんですね
entries.en:
Ah, now that you
mention it, you're
right. They finish
off a whale
before bringing it
ashore.

entries.jp: だからよ　龍馬の話は\n嘘っぱちだってんだよ
entries.en:
That's what I'm
saying. Ryoma's
story is a pack of
lies.

entries.jp: でも鯨に飲まれたって
entries.en: But he said he\nwas swallowed by\na whale...

entries.jp: わははは……\n正直言うと　ちょっぴり\n話を盛ったんじゃ
entries.en:
Wahahaha...
Truth is, I
stretched the
story a teeny bit.

entries.jp: 本当は漁師のおっさん達が\n面白がって　わしを\n鯨の口へ放り込んだんだ
entries.en:
What really
happened is the
fishermen
thought it'd be a
laugh and tossed
me into a whale's
mouth.

entries.jp: 山ほど鯨を食べるから\n一度食われてみるんじゃ！\nなんて　言われてな
entries.en:
They said, "You
eat heaps of
whale, so try
gettin' eaten for
once!"

entries.jp: ほれみろ\nとんだヨタ話じゃねえか
entries.en: See? What a load\nof tall tales.

entries.jp: でも面白い話でしたよ\n私も鯨の口の中に\n入ってみたいですね
entries.en:
But it was a fun
story. I'd like to
go inside a
whale's mouth
myself.

entries.jp: ロックを深く理解するには\n鯨に飲まれるのがいい\nシンディも飲まれてみ？
entries.en:
If ya wanna
understand rock
deep down,
gettin' swallowed
by a whale's the
way. Why
don'tcha try it,
Shindy?

entries.jp: はっ　またヨタかよ\nそんなことをしなくても\nオレ様のロックは最高だ
entries.en:
Hah, another tall
tale? Yours truly's
rock is already
the best without
any of that.

entries.jp: もっと高みに登れるかも\n知れないですよ　晋作
entries.en: You might be able\nto climb even\nhigher, Shinsaku.

entries.jp: あのなあ　桂さん\nお人好しもたいがいにしろ
entries.en:
Look,
Katsura-san.
Being a soft touch
only goes so far.

entries.jp: そうですかね？\n何事も体験だと思いますよ\n晋作
entries.en:
Do you think so? I
believe
everything is
worth
experiencing,
Shinsaku.

entries.jp: 既成概念に縛られていたら\n真のロックは難しいんじゃ\nないかと思うんです
entries.en:
If you're bound by
conventional
ideas, I think true
rock would be
difficult, don't
you?

entries.jp: はあ　お説教かよ\n付き合い切れねえ\nオレ様は湯を沸かしてくる
entries.en:
Ugh, a sermon? I
can't keep up.
Yours truly is
going to go heat
up a bath.

entries.jp: 龍馬のヨタ話を聞いてたら\n体中が生臭い気がしてきて\nたまらねえからな
entries.en:
Listening to
Ryoma's tall tales,
I feel like I smell
fishy all over. I
can't stand it.

entries.jp: ふふっ　晋作もヨタって\n言いながら　しっかり\n話を聞いてたんですね
entries.en:
Hehe. Shinsaku
kept calling it a
tall tale, but he
was listening
closely the whole
time.

entries.jp: ねえ　龍馬くん\nもっと聞かせて欲しいです\n土佐でのお話
entries.en:
Say, Ryoma-kun,
I'd love to hear
more stories
about Tosa.

entries.jp: おう　いくらでも話すぞ\n盛りは少なめで
entries.en:
Sure, I'll tell ya as
many as you like.
And I'll go easy
on the stretchin'.

entries.jp: 盛っていてもいいですよ\n龍馬くんのお話は楽しくて\nワクワクしますから
entries.en:
You can stretch
them all you like.
Your stories are
fun and exciting,
Ryoma-kun.

entries.jp: おう\nじゃあ盛り盛りで！
entries.en: All right! Then I'll\nstretch 'em as far\nas they go!

entries.jp:
こうして――
龍馬は高杉と桂に
懐かしい土佐での
思い出を語り続けた
entries.en:
And so, Ryoma
went on telling
Takasugi and
Katsura about his
fond memories of
Tosa.
